newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish navy ships to visit north Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Turkish navy ships to visit north Cyprus.

text.p: Turkish navy ships are to visit northern Cyprus soon in a show of solidarity with the breakaway Turkish Cypriot state, Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said.
"Acording to information I received from the general staff today, our warships will soon visit Cyprus," the Anatolian news agency quoted Erbakan as saying on Monday night.
"Turkey and Cyprus are tied to each other in every way. The whole world must know this and see it clearly," he said after meeting Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash.

Turkey has promised closer military and political links with the self-declared Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus in response to Greek Cypriot plans to install anti-aircraft missilies from Russia on the south of the island.

Ankara, whlch has 30,000 soldiers on Cyprus, has threatened to use force to halt the missile deployment. Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 in response to a Greek Cypriot coup backed by Athens.
